title: August and the Autopsy
premise: When a drowned man washes up in the marshes wearing clothes stolen from her own closet, insurance investigator Mirabel Montrose realizes the corpse is wearing the outfit she buried in a time capsule thirty years ago—and that someone is staging her memories as evidence. Her photographic recall of the town's old secrets makes her both the killer's archivist and their next target. As she unravels alibis woven by three families to protect a death everyone agreed to forget, Mirabel must choose between the loyalty that kept August Hollow quiet for decades and the truth that justice, even outside the law, demands a witness. In the end she exposes the conspiracy at the harvest festival, sparing the guilty daughter who acted out of love but forcing the town to finally bury its real secret.
about_author: Noor Vane is the pen name of a former small-town court stenographer who spent eleven years transcribing other people's confessions before writing her own stories. She lives near tidal marshes and keeps an alphabetized card catalog of unsolved cases she refuses to discuss at dinner parties.

chapters.title: The Wrong Clothes
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Called to assess a drowning claim, she recognizes the dead man's outfit instantly: it's hers, from a 1994 time capsule only five people knew about. The emotional beat is cold dread beneath professional calm—her invisibility has been weaponized, and the file she's kept on August Hollow opens itself.

chapters.title: Alphabet of Small Towns
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, flashback-laced. She walks the reader through her mental archive of Ashcombe's secrets while interviewing the widow, whose grief rings rehearsed. A torn photograph surfaces linking the victim to the old cannery fire. The beat: the past isn't buried; it's filed, waiting for someone with perfect recall.

chapters.title: Thirty Years of Quiet
chapters.summary: Sheriff Dane Okafor's POV. He knows Mirabel remembers too much and warns her off, revealing he was one of the five at the time capsule burial. His loyalty to the town wars with his duty to the badge. The beat: uneasy alliance—two keepers of secrets circling each other.

chapters.title: The Cannery Ledger
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Following insurance paper trails, she finds the victim was blackmailing descendants of the men who died in the 1994 cannery collapse—a collapse officially ruled accidental. Someone paid hush money through policies she herself once processed. Beat: guilt; her tidy files helped bury bodies.

chapters.title: What the Water Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating Mirabel and the killer's unnamed POV. The killer watches her investigate, admiring her memory while planning to use it—planting a second staged clue from the capsule. Mirabel dreams of the night of the burial and wakes remembering a sixth person under the dock. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Five Names, One Lie
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. She reconstructs the alibis of the four surviving capsule witnesses; all claim to have been together the night the victim died, but her memory catches a contradiction in a thirty-year-old statement. Sheriff Okafor quietly destroys a piece of evidence. Beat: betrayal—the law itself is part of the cover-up.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: Okafor's POV. He confesses to Mirabel that he falsified the 1994 report to protect Ruthie Vann, whose father caused the collapse and whose brother died covering it up. He asks Mirabel to let it stay buried. Beat: heartbreak—she loves him, or something like it, and must refuse him anyway.

chapters.title: The Sixth Witness
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, racing pace. The killer lures her to the drained capsule site: it's Ruthie Vann, avenging her brother by executing the blackmailers one by one, staging each scene with capsule relics so the town would finally look. She offers Mirabel a choice: witness or accomplice. Beat: the trap closes.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climax. At the festival where the whole town gathers, Mirabel publicly reconstructs the collapse, the cover-up, and the murders using her flawless memory—naming the dead, indicting the living, and stopping Ruthie mid-act before a third killing. Okafor arrests Ruthie with tears in his eyes. Beat: truth detonated in public.

chapters.title: Bury It Properly
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, resolution weeks later. The case reopens; the guilty fathers' names are carved onto the memorial; Okafor resigns rather than lie again, leaving a door open between them. Mirabel seals a new time capsule containing only the truth. Final beat: she stops being invisible—not famous, just finally seen.
